title: Morning Headlines
intro: A second consecutive night of US-Iran strikes, a worsening Ebola crisis in Congo, and surging oil prices signal one of the most turbulent Fridays of 2026.

items.title: US Strikes Iran for Second Night; Iran Fires Missiles at US Bases Across the Gulf
items.subtitle: Washington Post / Al Jazeera
items.summary: US forces struck roughly 90 Iranian military targets along the Strait of Hormuz coastline on Thursday night — a follow-up to 80-plus strikes the night before — while Iran retaliated by firing missiles and drones at US military installations in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar, effectively collapsing a fragile ceasefire and raising fears of broader regional war.

items.title: Congo Ebola Death Toll Hits 600 as Outbreak Spreads to New Provinces and Uganda
items.subtitle: Al Jazeera / Washington Times
items.summary: At least 600 people have now died in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak — the fastest-climbing death toll at any comparable point in outbreak history — with 1,759 confirmed cases now spreading beyond the initial northeastern zone into previously unaffected provinces and Uganda's capital Kampala; no approved vaccine exists for this Bundibugyo strain.

items.title: Oil Surges to Multi-Month Highs and Fed Rate-Hike Odds Jump to 70% as Iran War Rattles Markets
items.subtitle: Bloomberg / Rio Times Online
items.summary: Crude oil prices spiked to their highest level since spring as US-Iran fighting disrupted Strait of Hormuz shipping, while the 10-year US Treasury yield climbed to its highest since May; traders now price in roughly a 70% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike at the September meeting — up from 58% the day before — as energy-driven inflation fears mount.

items.title: France Beat Morocco 2-0 to Become World Cup 2026's First Semifinalist
items.subtitle: MSN / Euronews
items.summary: Les Bleus convincingly defeated Morocco 2-0 in the quarterfinals of the 2026 FIFA World Cup — hosted across the US, Canada, and Mexico — to advance to the last four, drawing enormous global viewership and setting up what is expected to be a blockbuster semifinal matchup.

items.title: Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham Expected to Succeed Keir Starmer as UK Labour Leader and Prime Minister
items.subtitle: World News Group / WORLD
items.summary: Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham has emerged as the clear frontrunner to take over as leader of the UK Labour Party and succeed Keir Starmer as Prime Minister, marking a significant generational shift in British politics that could reshape the government's domestic and foreign policy priorities.
